note: The recovered Step record's contract, machine-readable (kogaki#871).
src/review-draft.mjs READS these lists rather than restating them — this
file is the single carrier, so amending the record's shape is one edit and
never a two-copy divergence. The same arrangement src/record-schema.json
has with checks/check-proposal-contract.sh.
EVERY FIELD IS A FACT ABOUT THE PROSE, which is the whole design: a field
that could not be checked by pointing at the passage would be the reviewer
asserting rather than recovering, and the comparison downstream would have
nothing to bind to. That is why `forbidden_keys` exists — the reviewer
writes no verdicts and no advice, and a record carrying one is refused
rather than accepted-and-ignored, because an ignored field still shaped
the reading that produced the rest of the record.
`spans_lie_inside_the_step` is the second half of the same rule. A span is
a pair of DRAFT LINE NUMBERS — the coordinate the trace already uses, so a
reviewer, the Harness and a later reader all cite the same numbers — and
one pointing outside the passage is not evidence about the passage.
AN EMPTY ARRAY IS AN ANSWER AND AN ABSENT KEY IS NOT. `terms_introduced`,
`concessions` and `restates` are each legitimately empty for a passage
that introduces, concedes or repeats nothing — so they are REQUIRED and
may be `[]`. Making them optional would leave a reviewer who simply did
not look indistinguishable from one who looked and found none.
THE TOP-LEVEL KEY SET IS CLOSED, and `closed_key_set` below is where that
is declared rather than left to prose about it (kogaki#885, owner
selection 2026-09-06). `forbidden_keys` is an enumerated prohibition, and
an enumerated prohibition's load-bearing half is what happens to a name
nobody enumerated. Under a forbidden list alone that fallback is
admit-by-default, and it was INHERITED FROM THE MATCHER rather than
chosen: a record carrying `impression`, `assessment` or `confidence`
beside the seven passed, the Harness never read the key, and the
blindness this schema exists to hold was contaminated WITH NO TRACE.
The two arms fail in opposite directions and only one fails visibly. A
closed set refuses a reviewer who annotated harmlessly — but loudly, at
the validator, with the key named, and the repair is one edit. The
silent omission is the harmful one, so the set is closed. What closing
buys downstream is that the record's shape is TOTAL, which is what makes
the comparison's item table exhaustive: a key the Harness does not read
cannot silently carry a judgment.
The accepted cost, stated rather than discovered: a reviewer who wants to
annotate has nowhere to put it. That is deliberate — every field here is
a fact about the prose, and a field that could not be checked by pointing
at the passage would be the reviewer asserting rather than recovering.
THE DEPTHS ARE DIFFERENT ON PURPOSE. `forbidden_keys` is checked at every
depth; `closed_key_set` binds the TOP LEVEL only, because that is the
level whose vocabulary `required` declares. A nested object's admissible
keys are `fields.<name>.item_required`, which the per-field checks
already enforce, and closing depth against a list this file does not hold
would refuse on a name no declaration names.

claims.why_min: a passage asserting nothing is not a Step; an empty claims list is a reviewer who did not read rather than a passage with no content
